a: Screening: The screening period starts with the signature of informed consent and should end within approximately 28 days of starting leukapheresis. However, it may be extended if necessary to ensure an appropriate timeframe for medication washout or corticosteroid taper. Participant should re-sign informed consent if required per institutional policy.
b: Hospitalization: During Phase 1b, participants will be required to remain hospitalized post-LD through Day 7 or until all adverse events resolve to < grade 2 or baseline. Hospitalization in the phase 2 portion will be directed by the emerging safety data in phase 1b and per investigator discretion.
c: Demographics: Collection of demographic data and full date of birth given autologous CAR T treatment.
d: Medical history collection: This includes, but is not limited to, disease diagnosis, past treatment history, and significant other medical history that is not disease related.
e: Immunizations: Vaccination with seasonal influenza, SARS-CoV-2, and S. pneumoniae (20 valent) should be done following leukapheresis, when the corticosteroid dose is 15 mg/d prednisone equivalent or less and at least 2 weeks prior to LD. Revaccination should occur per protocol following B cell repletion (at day 90 or as required based on B cell repletion per individual patient). Participants with contraindications to vaccination should be discussed with the medical monitor.
f: Vital signs: systolic/diastolic blood pressure, pulse rate, respiration, body temperature, and O2 saturation. • On Days -5, -4, and -3, vital signs need to be checked within 1 hour ± 15 minutes before LD chemotherapy and 1 hour ± 15 minutes after LD chemo. • On Day 0, vital signs must be checked 15 ± 5 minutes before the infusion of C-CAR168, 15 ± 5 minutes during the infusion, and 15 ± 5 minutes after the infusion, until the vital signs are stable. • During hospitalization, vital signs should be recorded daily. • Temperature monitoring should continue every 6–8 hours following post-infusion monitoring through Day 14.
g: Physical examination, height, and weight: During the screening period, prior to LD, and at the time of withdrawal visit or completion of the 24-month visit, a complete physical examination is required. For other visits, the Investigator may conduct a limited symptom-directed physical examination. Body weight should be taken at every exam visit as well as prior to leukapheresis. The body weight on Day -5 should be used to calculate the BSA to determine dose of LD chemotherapy. Height will be measured only at screening.
h: MRI with MRS: MRI with MRS performed and read locally for clinical decision making and submitted per central imaging vendor specifications (see current imaging manual). [No matching row in current LN SoA — likely a cross-indication footnote.]
i: ICE Tool: Please see Appendix XX. If the patient is showing any symptoms of CRS or ICANs during hospitalization period, the ICE Tool should be performed daily.
j: Peripheral blood leukocyte collection (leukapheresis): This should be conducted according to current sponsor-provided Leukapheresis Manual and per institutional standards.
k: LD chemotherapy: Cyclophosphamide (300 mg/m²/d) and fludarabine (25 mg/m²/d) should be administered on Days -5, -4, and -3 over approximately 30-minute infusion.
l: PROs: All participants will be asked to complete the following questionnaires at each visit: VAS, EQ-5D-5L, GAD-7, PHQ-9.
m: Neurocognitive Testing: MMSE (Mini-Mental State Exam), MoCA (Montreal Cognitive Assessment), VAS, SDMT, ANAM and PROMIS (SPMSep, depression, anxiety) batteries. [No matching row in current LN SoA — likely a cross-indication footnote.]
n: Pregnancy testing: For female participants of childbearing potential, a serum pregnancy test will be performed per the SOA.
o: PK, PD, and exploratory endpoint-related laboratory assessments: Tube and sample specification will be provided in the current laboratory manual(s). After 28 days, if 2 consecutive test results are negative, sample collection may be discontinued.
p: If all post-treatment assays for an individual participant are negative during the first year, collection of the yearly follow-up samples may be discontinued for that individual and yearly review of the medical history will generally be sufficient for the participant.
q: Only AEs/SAEs directly related to study therapy are to be recorded during follow up (see safety reporting periods table).
r: Only concomitant therapies administered for AEs directly related to investigational product should be recorded during the follow up period.
